title: Detailed Inspection of the Fin Box Root Rib and its Lateral Load Introduction

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Detailed inspection of the fin box root rib and the lateral load introduction into the rear fuselage, covering the fastener rows, the shear ties and the eddy current inspection of the rib flange radii.

sections.purpose: This task inspects the fin box root rib and its attachment to the rear fuselage, and does the eddy current inspection of the rib flange radii that is the primary means of finding a crack at the lateral load introduction.
sections.job_setup_note: The rudder must be removed and the fin leading edge opened for access. The inspection is done from a tail dock; working from a ladder does not give the access needed for the eddy current probe to be held square. Record the flight cycles at the time of inspection, because the finding history for this location is expressed in cycles and not in calendar time.
sections.procedure: 1. Record the aircraft flight cycles. 2. Remove the rudder and open the fin leading edge. WARNING: THE TAIL DOCK MUST BE SECURED AND THE AIRCRAFT MUST NOT BE MOVED WHILE PERSONNEL ARE IN THE FIN. 3. Get access to zones 321, 322 and 323. 4. Clean the root rib area and remove the sealant from the fastener rows. 5. Do a detailed visual inspection of the rib flange over the full span, with particular attention to the three lower stations. 6. Inspect the shear tie D5530110749890 at each lower station for cracking at the fillet radius. 7. Inspect the splice plate D5530119339028 and the strap D5530113880239 where fitted for fretting at the faying surface. CAUTION: FRETTING PRODUCT AT A FAYING SURFACE IS NOT A REPORTABLE FINDING BY ITSELF, BUT IT MUST NOT BE CLEANED OFF BEFORE THE EDDY CURRENT INSPECTION. IT MARKS THE POSITION TO EXAMINE MOST CLOSELY. 8. Do a high frequency eddy current inspection of the rib flange radii along both fastener rows. 9. Do a low frequency eddy current inspection of the second layer at the three lower stations. 10. Record every indication with its station and its length. 11. Check the anchor nuts AES147323-7D in the rib flange for security where the bolted strap is fitted. 12. Check the skin panel ORD555543-03 at the rib termination for cracking at the run-out. 13. Compare the findings with drawings D55301101338 and D55301155365 and report any indication to engineering before the fin is closed.
sections.close_out: Restore the sealant over the fastener rows and reinstate the protection scheme on any bare material. Close the fin leading edge and reinstall the rudder, then do the rudder travel check. Record the flight cycles, the eddy current settings and every indication on the maintenance record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 11 applies to aircraft with the bolted lateral load strap only.

safety_precautions: Secure the tail dock and do not move the aircraft with personnel in the fin.
Do not clean off fretting product before the eddy current inspection.

tooling.reference: Eddy current set with high and low frequency probes
